methodology.title: 2.1 Core Principle: Science CLIL Integration
content: Problem: Students know random animal names (dog, snake, frog) but lack the academic vocabulary to classify them logically.

Solution: We explicitly teach 5 scientific classifications (mammal, reptile, amphibian, insect, bird) linked directly to their defining physical traits (hair, scales, smooth skin, six legs, feathers) using the Present Simple tense for universal facts.

methodology.title: 2.2 Session Flow (120 Minutes)
content: Session 1: Introduce the 5 animal groups and their core physical characteristics. Focus on matching groups to traits.
Session 2: Apply classifications to real-world examples. Practice distinguishing tricky animals.
Session 3: Full production. Write a scientific report classifying multiple animals and present it orally.

methodology.title: 2.4 Teacher Notes: Pull-Out Tasks & Communicative Task
content: S1 pull-out: Show a picture of an animal (e.g., a snake). Student must classify it and state its defining trait ("It is a reptile. It has scales.").

Communicative task (Step 5 - 10 min): The Animal Sorting Game. Student A has a list of animal traits. Student B has the animal group names. They must ask and answer questions to match them up perfectly.

parts.title: PART 1: READING INPUT  Max Visits the Zoo
content: Scientists group animals by their features.
Mammals have fur and feed their babies milk — a dog, a whale, and a bat are all mammals!

Then, he watched a tiny ant on a green leaf. The ant is an insect with six legs.
Finally, he saw a colorful parrot. The parrot is a bird with beautiful feathers.
Max loves being a nature detective!

games.materials: Vocab flashcards W38: mammal, reptile, amphibian, insect, bird
instructions: Round 1: Teacher calls a Vietnamese meaning — first student to say the English word AND use it correctly in a sentence wins the card.
Round 2: Reverse — teacher calls English word, student gives Vietnamese + memory trick.
Bonus round: Students chain all vocab words (mammal, reptile, amphibian, insect, bird) into one connected story using sequence connectors from this week.
Team variant: 2 teams, 10 cards per round. Team with highest score wins.

games.name: Grammar Relay
games.session_fit: Best in Drill slot (Slot 2) or after P4/P6 in 3-session mode
games.materials: 10 sentence cards — 5 correct, 5 with errors based on: Present Simple for facts (has/have, lays, lives)
instructions: Grammar focus this week: Present Simple for facts (has/have, lays, lives).
Speed Read: Display sentence for 5 sec. Teams write C (correct) or E (error) on whiteboards simultaneously — no copying allowed.
Fix-It: For error sentences, team that corrects fastest AND explains the rule earns double points.
Build: Each team member adds 1 original sentence using the grammar target. The chain must be logically connected — each sentence must link to the previous.

games.name: Story Race
games.session_fit: All formats — best in final slot of the week (S3 / Slot 5 / Session B)
games.materials: Story starter card: theme "Nature's Rules — Animal Groups"
instructions: Give each pair a story starter connected to this week's theme: "Nature's Rules — Animal Groups".
Pair A adds 2 sentences — must include at least 2 vocab words from this week.
Pass to Pair B: they MUST correct any grammar mistake from Pair A first, then add 2 more sentences using different vocab words.
Final round: Each pair presents their story ending aloud. Class votes on most creative + most accurate (mammal, reptile, amphibian, insect, bird usage). Teacher scores grammar precision.

listening_script.text: Hello, animal experts! Today we are sorting animals into five groups. A dog is a mammal. It has fur and feeds its babies with milk. A snake is a reptile. It has scales and lives on land. A frog is an amphibian. It lives both in water and on land. A bee is an insect. It has six legs and three body parts. An eagle is a bird. It has feathers and lays eggs. Remember to use 'has', 'lays', or 'lives' when you describe animals!

listening_script.text: Welcome to my animal science presentation! I will explain the five animal groups. First, mammals: a whale is a mammal because it has warm blood and feeds its babies milk. Second, reptiles: a crocodile is a reptile because it has scales and lays eggs. Third, amphibians: a salamander lives in water and on land, so it is an amphibian. Every animal belongs to a group based on its features!
